verdict.line: You lose it if you eat free Boomerang Throw poke before level 6 and let Gnar hit max Rage unanswered; you win it by diving right after he reverts to mini form and cashing in your measured solo-kill edge.

brief.thesis: This matchup sits dead even at 48.4% over 1517 games, and the entire fight is gated by Gnar's Rage meter rather than levels or items. Mini Gnar is a safe poke bot with Boomerang Throw and no hard CC; Mega Gnar gets a stun off W (Wallop) and, once his R (GNAR!) ultimate ranks up, a wall-stun knockback that turns him into the all-in threat. Jax's job is to pick fights in the window where Gnar has none of that online.

theirWindow.when: Gnar's Rage bar is nearly full
theirWindow.what: He's about to transform into Mega Gnar and gain W (Wallop)'s stun, plus R (GNAR!)'s wall-stun knockback once it's ranked. Don't half-commit into the transform — either disengage before it pops or go in with E (Counter Strike) already up so you can no-sell his follow-up autos and stun him back.

yourWindow.when: Right after Gnar reverts to mini form
yourWindow.what: His Rage resets to zero, so he has no Wallop stun and no GNAR! knockback for a stretch. Dive with W (Empower) into Q (Leap Strike), then lock the duel down with E (Counter Strike) before his Rage bar refills.

start.why: Measured as the stronger start (48.8% over 962 games, 53.3% pick) and it directly answers Boomerang Throw's poke damage, which is the only thing mini Gnar can do to you before level 6.

boots.why: Takes the 71.8% pick rate at 48.1% win over 1207 games; Gnar's entire kit — autos, Boomerang Throw, Boulder Toss — is physical damage, so flat armor beats the magic-resist boots here.

core.why: Highest-winrate path (58.7% over 121 games); the attack speed and damage proc feed directly into R (Relentless Assault)'s every-third-hit bonus, so your trades scale fastest with this first.
Follows Trinity in the top build path; its proc rewards the exact stun-into-auto pattern E (Counter Strike) sets up.
Closes out the highest-winrate core (58.7%); lets you survive the burst window if a fight goes long against Mega Gnar's GNAR! knockback.

situational.when: gnar's team starts stacking burst to punish you for diving into his all-in window
gnar builds toward a tankier mega-form skirmisher and you need sustained DPS instead of burst
the game goes long and you need the extra stat payoff on top of trinity's spike

runes.keystoneWhy: This page runs a notably higher 51.2% win rate (18% pick) than the Lethal Tempo page's 44.3%, and it fits the structural problem here: Jax has no ranged poke answer to Boomerang Throw before level 6, so sustain through Grasp's proc matters more than attack speed scaling that only pays off once you're already ahead.

summoners.why: Flash + Teleport is the highest-winrate combo measured (51%, 32.4% pick). Teleport lets you reset the wave and come back in after a mini-Gnar poke exchange instead of being stuck on a lost lane, and Flash is what dodges Boomerang Throw or repositions out of a GNAR! knockback once Gnar's ultimate is up.

playing.title: Trade through autos with E
playing.detail: E (Counter Strike) dodges all incoming basic attacks for its duration, then stuns and damages surrounding enemies. If mini Gnar tries to kite-auto you at range 300 or closer, pop it to no-sell the damage and stun him on the follow-up.

playing.title: Punish right after he reverts
playing.detail: The moment Mega Gnar reverts to mini, his Rage resets to zero and he loses Wallop's stun and GNAR!'s knockback. Dive immediately with W (Empower) into Q (Leap Strike) while he has no CC to answer with.

playing.title: Save E for his Hop landing
playing.detail: Gnar's E (Hop, range 475) bounces him off your head and travels further — it's not evasive once he's committed to landing on you. Counter Strike right as he lands to lock him down.

playing.title: Track the Rage bar all lane
playing.detail: It's the single tell for this matchup: full bar means Wallop's stun and eventually GNAR!'s wall-stun are live. Don't extend a trade into a Gnar sitting on max Rage.

playing.title: Respect GNAR! once it's rank 3+
playing.detail: R (GNAR!)'s cooldown is 90/60/30/0/0s — at rank 3 it's already down to 30 seconds and becomes free at rank 4. From level 11 onward, assume he can throw you into a wall for a bonus-damage stun on a short timer.

playing.title: Empower your leaps, not your autos
playing.detail: W (Empower) buffs your next attack or Leap Strike. Save it for Q (Leap Strike) to open trades — the bonus damage plus the hit to nearby enemies lands before Gnar can disengage.

playing.title: Rush Trinity before matching his power spikes
playing.detail: Trinity Force first is the highest-winrate path in the data (58.7%); it directly fuels R (Relentless Assault)'s attack-speed stacking, so finishing it before Gnar's ultimate ranks up is what converts your solo-kill edge into real gold.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1) — not assumptions. The mechanical reasoning (Rage-bar timing, ability interactions, trade sequencing) is this brief's own tactical read on top of that data, not a measured stat.
